extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, reviewers, and educated readers evaluating books on literature, science, and religion
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance for writing or judging reviews and arguments about the relations among literature, science, art, and religion — what counts as sound method, convincing proof, and constructive tone. Emphasizes the distinctive methods of literary and scientific culture and criteria for a successful critical book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary method (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: By literature we mean, and rightly mean, the study of books of language, of the arts of expression and criticism, and familiarity with the most perfect written productions, as such, whether in prose or poetry, that have been produced in all time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat literature as training in study of written works, expression, and criticism; evaluate claims that attempt to expand this method beyond its traditional objects with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific method (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essence of the scientific method is the actual study of things — observing, analyzing, and comparing the actual facts — arising in revolt against mere verbal studies, involving new objects, new procedures, and new disciplines of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize science as an independent, systematic culture grounded in experience and experiment; arguments about science must acknowledge its empirical procedures and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate literary and scientific methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Without asserting that the relations of these two methods of culture are essentially antagonistic, it remains true that they are so profoundly different that they are not to be confounded or identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating one method as merely a subset of the other; evaluate attempts to 'incorporate' or 'absorb' one method into the other skeptically and test whether key procedures or aims are being ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense for truth as a distinct cultural demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Arnold nowhere speaks of the sense for truth, and this, obviously because truth, as an object of feeling, does not enter into the literary ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing cultural education proposals, check whether they address not only beauty and conduct but also the human demand for truth — particularly if they claim parity between literary and scientific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific culture requires practical acquaintance with phenomena (no 'sham science')
rubrics_metrics.description: That which is obtained from books alone, without an acquaintance with phenomena, is not true science but sham science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate claims of scientific understanding by whether the author or curriculum includes empirical training, observation, and experiment rather than purely bookish treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial competence and awareness of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Arnold is quite aware of the slenderness and deficiency of his own scientific attainments. But, had he been more perfectly aware of them, he would hardly have ventured upon this mode of escaping from the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics/authors should acknowledge their expertise limits; weigh arguments more heavily when the author demonstrates command of the subject-matter and its methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require proof for claims of superiority between methods
rubrics_metrics.description: He expatiates on the utilities of literature, but he offers no proof that its past ascendency is still justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a work asserts the superiority of one cultural method over another, demand concrete proof (historical, empirical, practical) rather than assertion or rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid widening definitions without adequate conception
rubrics_metrics.description: He would even so widen it as to include all science... That is, science disappears as a separate intellectual interest by its complete absorption in literature: neat but unsatisfactory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of rhetorical redefinitions that subsume distinct domains; evaluate whether the wider definition preserves essential characteristics of the absorbed field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sympathy and fair handling of opposing views
rubrics_metrics.description: He lacks sympathy with one of the sides... he adopts a tone toward the adherents of supernatural religion which is, to say the least of it, by no means conciliatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reconciliatory or synthetic works ('eirenicon'), assess whether the author displays sympathetic understanding of both parties; lack of sympathy weakens attempts at reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate appreciation of subfields (e.g., music and the arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: He almost invariably regards art as solely dealing with beautiful objects of sight... We have throughout observed not one word devoted to music, yet there are thousands nowadays with whom the cultus of rhythmic and harmonic sounds has usurped the place of almost all other worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comprehensive treatment of 'art' or 'culture' should address relevant sub-disciplines; omission of significant arts (like music) is a substantive gap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality and actionable proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The second or 'practical' part of the book is not practical in any sense that leads to action. It merely shows that the natural religion which is his theme is new in action among us in influencing men's lives. It may set men thinking, it cannot bid them to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work purports to offer practical solutions, evaluate whether its recommendations lead to concrete action or remain purely contemplative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, candor, and lucid expression
rubrics_metrics.description: He is candid and clear-sighted, and sees distinctly that what he calls religion will be called in turn pantheism and paganism by 'religious' people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise clarity and candor when authors plainly state their positions and limitations; clarity helps readers judge claims fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of acute social diagnosis and memorable phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Take ... the power of acute social diagnosis that is throughout displayed... joined to this power of observation is found the power of expressing its results in short, pithy phrases or sentences that stick in the memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a work's value partly by its diagnostic insight into social conditions and by the effectiveness of its language (concise, memorable formulations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between emphasizing commonalities and acknowledging divergences
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of the author, which is to point out the large amount of agreement among conflicting parties, is perfectly legitimate, and permits a certain exaggeration in looking only at common qualities, and neglecting divergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that emphasizing agreement can be useful, but a sound critical work should also register and analyze real divergences rather than elide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of classification and discrimination (conceptual clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three different phases of atheism ... are excellently discriminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise clear taxonomies and discriminations that illuminate confusing debates; conceptual clarity is a mark of strong analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess probable reception among stakeholder groups
rubrics_metrics.description: It remains to discuss its probable effect on the two parties between whom, in a measure, it attempts to effect a reconciliation... The religious world will regard its religion as having been misunderstood, and not sympathized with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reviewer should consider and report how different audiences are likely to receive the work and whether its rhetorical strategy will persuade or alienate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether author achieves intended reform or synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: No eirenicon can be effected between two opposing schools by inducing them to adopt the same name on their banners. It is by bringing into full consciousness the thoughts and feelings of modern men that this book will exercise its chief influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work aims at reconciliation or reform, judge whether its method (e.g., renaming, moral exhortation, empirical argument) is adequate to accomplish substantive synthesis or change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider tone and emotional effect on reader
rubrics_metrics.description: His words are wise but sad; it has not been given him to fire them with faith, but only to light them with reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the author's tone (e.g., depressing vs inspiring) and the emotional effect this will have on readership; tone influences persuasiveness and practical impact.
